# Loupe

> Loupe is an open-source, embeddable visual-feedback SDK. Product managers inspect any element on a live product, pin a comment, and capture a screenshot; comments persist, re-anchor across redeploys, and are handed to Claude Code as an actionable backlog via the Model Context Protocol (MCP). MIT licensed, written in TypeScript.

## What it does
- Embeds a Shadow-DOM widget in any web product (npm package or script tag).
- Lets authorized users inspect a DOM element and attach a comment + screenshot, drag a free-size region to screenshot, screen-record a region to video (webm, via getDisplayMedia), or drop a "free" page-level note anywhere (no element, no screenshot).
- The control is a dockable DevTools-style panel with a sidebar of built-in pages (Home + Comments + Activity) plus any the host registers via `init({ tabs })` (a worked example ships as `connectTab()`). Home leads with stat tiles (Open / Needs you / Resolved / Stale), scope chips carrying this-page and whole-project counts, a project manager (link the page to a repo from a host-supplied searchable list; add/validate environment URLs) and the most recent feedback; Comments holds the capture tools and the list (grouped by day in the project scope); Activity is a live monitor — status dot, collapsible session summary, tool chips and an event feed fed by `trackActivity()` (Loupe's own operations included) that says "monitor unavailable" when nothing is connected. The header carries a position menu (left/bottom/right/float), a theme toggle, a settings dropdown (five accent colours, hover-hints/markers/page-paths switches, Restart tour, and the running package version + server/offline mode), and a minimize button. Dock it to an edge (which pushes the host page over) or float it as a movable, resizable window; it collapses to a FAB cluster and becomes a bottom sheet on mobile. A five-step guided tour runs once on first open (skippable, replayable), and each view shows a one-time contextual hint card. Position, theme, accent, scope, tab, minimize state, marker visibility, hint and tour state all persist.
- Threads carry a lifecycle: a comment can record the pull request carrying its fix (`pr: { number, url, state, checksPassed, checksTotal }`), which renders as a chip (Sent to agent → In PR → Review preview → Reviewed) plus a monospace PR link and a checks meter. Threads in In Review lead with a review banner (Approve / Add comment) and an origin toggle that shows the original request beside Claude's proposed change. Only a human resolves a thread; an agent moves work to In Review.
- Generates and iterates on a change in-panel: `init({ generate })` adds a Generate pane with a sandboxed preview, an opacity comparison against the original, undo, prev/next iteration history and a refine/revise input; local-AI endpoint + model are configurable with a real connection check against an OpenAI-compatible `/v1/models`. Without a generator the pane offers an access request via `init({ onRequestAccess })`.
- Agent navigation is consent-gated: `requestNavigation(url, { reason, requester })` shows the user who wants to go where and why, and nothing navigates without an explicit grant (only http(s) is even offerable); decisions are kept as an audit trail. Dictation (`SpeechRecognition`) is available in the composer where supported.
- The MCP server hosts a local bridge on 127.0.0.1:9800 (LOUPE_BRIDGE_PORT, 0 disables): element selections POST to /selection and read back from /selection/latest and /selection/history; agents register at /agents with a heartbeat and are evicted after 30s of silence; /events and /thread-updates are Server-Sent Events channels carrying selections, agent changes and thread updates (update_status and propose_change publish to them). CORS is limited to chrome-extension and loopback origins, and a busy port is logged and skipped rather than fatal.
- Commits and opens pull requests on GitHub: a multi-file fix lands as one atomic commit (Git Data API), the token resolves from GITHUB_TOKEN/GH_TOKEN or `gh auth token`, placeholders are detected rather than sent, and errors are redacted. Working branches track which branch accumulates a repo's fixes (with a running fix count) plus its PR and preview URL; per-repo URL patterns (`*` within a segment, `**` across) let a deployment be recognised, and a preview lookup probes candidates - reported URL, then patterns, then the GitHub Pages `pr-preview/pr-N` convention - answering "not ready" rather than guessing.
- Fixes land on ONE working branch per repo rather than one PR per comment: create_pr_for_thread accumulates commits and keeps a table of every fix and its commit in the PR body, starting a fresh branch when the tracked PR is merged or closed (a revision always gets its own revision-* branch). Threads are conversations: mark_thread_addressed moves a thread to In Review and has NO status parameter, so an agent cannot resolve one; add_thread_message replies without changing status; the comment body is message #1 and replies carry authors typed user/agent/guest.
- Threads are conversations in the panel: expanding one shows the replies (an agent's reply carries a left accent bar and an agent tag), an optimistic reply composer that keeps a failed reply on screen with a Retry, an activity timeline derived from the thread's own state (captured -> replied -> change ready -> PR opened -> preview live -> waiting on a human -> resolved, with skipped steps absent), and Copy thread text (a readable summary leading with the element selector). Replies load lazily per expanded card; participants are recorded on write and the thread's author is folded in on read.
- Integrations: Slack and Telegram post thread lifecycle events (created, agent working, PR created, resolved) to mapped channels. Credentials are AES-256-GCM encrypted at rest, never returned by the API, and require LOUPE_CREDENTIAL_KEY. Delivery retries 3x with backoff and logs every attempt. Admin-only endpoints under /v1/integrations.
- The panel has a Chat page: a gather tray collects several elements/screenshots into one message (order matters, items can be excluded), plus Web Speech dictation and an unread badge. The bridge serves a read-only activity dashboard at /monitor with a live timeline, sessions, tool usage and files touched, plus get_recent_events, get_files_touched and get_dashboard_url tools. Bridge SSE events are NAMED — listen with addEventListener, not onmessage.
- Companion chat: send a message to the agent mid-task and every pending message is prepended to the next tool result (take/ack, so delivery is exactly once and a failed tool never consumes one). Tools: get_companion_messages, reply_to_companion. Agent instrumentation: an opt-in, idempotent Claude Code hooks installer, a bounded event store, and sessions folded from events (get_activity_summary).
- A reply can carry its own attachments (images/video), and retracting one is a soft delete: the row survives with deleted_at set, is excluded from the default message list, and is available via ?includeDeleted=1. New replies and retractions relay thread-update events over the agent bridge, env-gated on LOUPE_BRIDGE_URL.
- Reactions: emoji on a reply, with counts and per-user state. The database primary key is the toggle invariant (reacting twice cannot create two rows) and the toggle is idempotent in both directions. Presence: who else has the page open, heartbeats with a 20s TTL, rendered as an avatar cluster; hidden when no bridge is configured.
- Mentions: @name in a reply is parsed (emails, code spans and trailing punctuation excluded), resolved against everyone who has taken part, and notified in-app; unresolved handles are reported rather than dropped. A "Needs you" predicate in shared flags a thread in review, an agent's unanswered question or a failed run, and deliberately excludes threads an agent is still working on.
- Stores comments in Postgres and screenshots/recordings in object storage.
- Re-anchors each pin to its element after redeploys using a multi-signal fingerprint.
- Exposes an MCP server (tools: list_comments, get_comment, propose_change, update_status) so Claude Code reads feedback with full element context — the screenshot is delivered as an image — and writes its modified HTML/CSS back via propose_change, which the dashboard renders as code plus a live before/after preview for the dev team.
- Ships a Kanban triage dashboard and an MV3 browser extension (pixel-perfect capture on any site).
- Optional Loupe Hub: a hosted service where organization owners (Google sign-in) manage allowed members and projects; it verifies HMAC-signed issues (POST /v1/issues), checks the author's email belongs to the organization, and forwards them to a per-project signed webhook. The Laravel package forwards new comments to Hub when LOUPE_HUB_URL, LOUPE_PROJECT_ID and LOUPE_PROJECT_SECRET are set.
